items.claim: 24:3-4 reads as one continuous house-building image (house built, then its rooms filled) rather than two unrelated maxims, which supports the proverb_cluster call even though the row's own "shared vocabulary" framing overstates the lexical evidence.
items.evidence: v3 בְּ֭חָכְמָה יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֑יִת ('through wisdom a house is built') opens the figure and v4 וּ֭בְדַעַת חֲדָרִ֣ים יִמָּלְא֑וּ ('and by knowledge, rooms are filled') completes it; "house" (v3-only) and "rooms" (v4-only) never repeat as a shared token, so the cited "shared vocabulary" is inaccurate as stated, but the cohesion is real on a stronger ground the row did not name: rooms are only intelligible as part of the house just built (part-whole pair grouping, not catchword repetition). No undisclosed catchword crosses the v2|v3 seam (checked, none). The v4|v5 seam does share the token da'at (knowledge) but sweep.py --skel on that token returns 44/915 verses book-wide -- too common a wisdom-vocabulary term to carry independent cross-seam weight, so not raised as a defect.

items.claim: The row's stated ground for clustering 24:5-6 -- "the strength/power vocabulary carrying across both verses" -- is not byte-true: v6 contains no strength/power term at all, so the named catchword evidence fails verification.
items.evidence: v5 גֶּֽבֶר חָכָ֥ם בַּע֑וֹז וְאִֽישׁ דַּ֝֗עַת מְאַמֶּץ כֹּֽחַ carries the strength/power terms oz and koach; v6 כִּ֣י בְ֭תַחְבֻּלוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה לְּךָ֣ מִלְחָמָ֑ה ('for by strategies you wage war') shifts entirely to war/counsel vocabulary -- neither oz, koach, nor any strength synonym recurs. The claimed "vocabulary carrying across" does not survive a token check. A different, genuinely available ground was left unnamed: v6 opens with ki, the same declarative-plus-ki-motive construction the sibling admonition_unit rows in this span (24:11-12, 24:15-16, 24:19-20) explicitly cite as their cohesion evidence. The row should have named that construction instead of the false vocabulary claim; as submitted the proverb_cluster grounds do not meet the byte-grounded-cohesion bar.

items.claim: The scheme-root catchword is genuine and rare: zimmah links 24:8 to 24:9, and this is the row's own correctly-named, byte-grounded proverb_cluster ground.
items.evidence: v8 בַּֽעַל מְזִמּ֥וֹת ('a man of schemes') and v9 זִמַּ֣ת אִוֶּ֣לֶת חַטָּ֑את ('the scheme of folly is sin') share the root zmm. sweep.py --skel on that consonant cluster returns only 13/915 verses book-wide, and 24:8-24:9 is the only adjacent pair in the whole book, confirming a genuine rather than coincidental catchword. No undisclosed shared token crosses either neighboring seam (v7|v8 or v9|v10, both checked, neither shares a token).

items.claim: The imperative-plus-answered-excuse structure is byte-correct and both boundaries (with 24:10 and 24:13) are clean, with no undisclosed shared token at either seam.
items.evidence: v11 הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת opens a fresh Hiphil imperative after v10's declarative maxim (הִ֭תְרַפִּיתָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָ֗ה, no imperative, no shared root with v11); v12 opens "כִּֽי תֹאמַ֗ר" ('for you say') and later in the same verse asks "הֲֽלֹא" ('does he not [weigh hearts]'), together answering the anticipated excuse as claimed. v13 אֱכָל בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ opens a fresh vocative sharing no token with v12's closing kefo'olo. The rejected_alternative (v12 as a detached single_proverb on divine judgment) is the strongest real rival here and is correctly defeated by the excuse-answer link.

items.claim: The vocative-plus-purpose-clause unit is byte-correct, the petuchah at 24:14 is used only as corroboration (not as a driver), and the near-verbatim recurrence at 23:18 is accurately disclosed as non-adjacent texture rather than merger grounds.
items.evidence: v13 אֱכָל בְּנִ֣י דְבַ֣שׁ (vocative) plus v14 כֵּ֤ן דְּעֶ֥ה חָכְמָ֗ה ...(purpose clause) confirmed at the byte tier. The petuchah at Prov.24.14 is confirmed single-witness in pmarks_Prov.json and is correctly framed as corroboration, never as the boundary driver. The clause וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת ('your hope will not be cut off') at 24:14 matches וְ֝תִקְוָתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תִכָּרֵֽת at 23:18 on the core wording (byte-confirmed), and the row correctly holds this as non-adjacent texture rather than using it to merge rows.

items.claim: The direct-address-prohibition-plus-motive structure is byte-correct, and the petuchah-at-24:14 disclosure is symmetric with the neighboring row, with no defect on this row's own stated grounds.
items.evidence: v15 אַל תֶּאֱרֹ֣ב רָ֭שָׁע (prohibition) plus v16 כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨בַע יִפּ֣וֹל ...(ki-motive, righteous-falls/wicked-overthrown antithesis) confirmed. The petuchah at 24:14 is disclosed identically by this row and by its neighboring row (symmetry satisfied per the campaign's mark-disclosure rule). The rejected_alternative (v16 as a detached single_proverb) is correctly defeated by the motive-clause link to v15's prohibition. A rare shared root (kashal, 6/915 verses book-wide) does cross this row's own forward seam into 24:17; it is not raised again here since it bears on the 24:17-24:18 row's own "unrelated" claim, not on this row's stated grounds.

items.claim: The claim that 24:17 "opens a fresh prohibition unrelated to the wicked-man-ambush warning just closed" is contradicted by a rare, byte-verified shared root: kashal links 24:16 and 24:17, and the fall-root echoes as well, so the row's rejected_alternative addresses only the weaker forward rival and never engages this stronger backward link.
items.evidence: v16 closes יִכָּשְׁל֥וּ ('are overthrown') and v17 opens with בִּנְפֹ֣ל ...(same fall-root) and continues וּ֝בִכָּשְׁל֗וֹ ('and when he stumbles'). sweep.py --skel on the kashal consonant cluster returns exactly 6/915 verses book-wide (4:12, 4:19, 16:18, 24:16, 24:17, 26:1), and 24:16-24:17 is the only adjacent pair -- a genuine, rare catchword. The fall-root also echoes (v16 yippol / v17 binfol), same verb, though at the skeleton-substring tier only binfol registers (sweep.py --skel nafal = 2/915: 24:17, 30:18) because the imperfect assimilates the initial nun -- disclosed here at the root/lexical tier, not the skeleton tier. Neither this row nor its neighbor discloses this cross-seam link, and the row's rejected_alternative only tests merging forward with 24:19-20 (a weak rival, cleanly defeated by v19's fresh doubled imperative); the stronger backward rival -- that v17-18 continues rather than breaks from v15-16's wicked-man scene -- is never engaged. The ketiv/qere at v17's object (אויביך אֽ֭וֹיִבְךָ) is otherwise correctly disclosed.

items.claim: The doubled-prohibition-plus-motive structure is byte-correct, and the al tekanne bracket back to 24:1 is an exact, correctly-disclosed non-adjacent echo used only as texture, not as merger grounds.
items.evidence: v19 אַל תִּתְחַ֥ר בַּמְּרֵעִ֑ים אַל תְּ֝קַנֵּ֗א and v20's ki-motive כִּ֤י לֹֽא תִהְיֶ֣ה אַחֲרִ֣ית ...(no reward for evil, lamp of the wicked snuffed out) confirmed. אַל תְּ֭קַנֵּא ('do not envy') at v19 is byte-identical to Prov.24.1's opening prohibition (confirmed at the oshb tier), correctly treated as a distant bracketing echo rather than boundary evidence, since the two occurrences are 18 verses apart and every intervening row already stands on its own grounds. No undisclosed shared token crosses the 24:18|24:19 seam beyond the common root ra'a' (evil), which is too high-frequency in this book to carry independent catchword weight.
